question: Tracheostomy is a planned surgical procedure performed at the 2nd-3rd tracheal rings, whereas cricothyroidotomy is an emergency procedure performed through the cricothyroid membrane when tracheostomy cannot be performed in time.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Tracheostomy is a planned procedure at the 2nd-3rd tracheal rings; cricothyroidotomy is the emergency rescue airway through the cricothyroid membrane. The two procedures address different clinical scenarios and use anatomically distinct entry points.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is the definitive distinction. Tracheostomy = controlled, theatre-based, 2nd-3rd ring, definitive airway. Cricothyroidotomy = emergency, cricothyroid membrane, temporising rescue airway when 'can't intubate, can't oxygenate'.
